divergences.old: openshift namespace usage --csv printing raw CSV to stdout instead of the envelope
divergences.toil: --csv writes the CSV to a file in the workspace named with --out <file>, never overwriting, and data is the JSON result with the saved absolute path added as file. Nothing but the envelope goes to stdout
divergences.why: Every command writes exactly one envelope; CSV goes to a file only (decision 4 on #68).

divergences.old: openshift namespace usage with no --out flag
divergences.toil: --out <file> is added, and --csv requires it (and --out requires --csv), checked before any request
divergences.why: Where the CSV goes has to be named, since it no longer goes to stdout (decision 4 on #68).

divergences.old: Named clusters as openshift.environments.<env>.instances.<instance>.{baseUrl, token} beside flat openshift.baseUrl and openshift.token, with openshift.defaultEnvironment and openshift.defaultInstance picking one; --env or a default environment with no instance (or the reverse) failing, naming the missing flag
divergences.toil: Each cluster is an openshift connection, with env and instance settings for a named one. --env and --instance each select the connection named <name>, or the one whose env (or instance) setting is <name>, and must agree when both are given; either alone is enough when it identifies one connection, the two together pick the one connection matching both when each alone matches several, and a value that still matches several is INVALID_INPUT naming them. defaults.openshift.connection takes the place of defaultEnvironment and defaultInstance. An unknown name is INVALID_INPUT listing the clusters toil knows
divergences.why: toil's config is a set of named connections, and --env is the one environment concept that selects among them (decision 9 on #68), so clusters can't be a nested map inside one connection.

divergences.old: With openshift.defaultEnvironment and openshift.defaultInstance set, the stored cluster's baseUrl and token winning over the OPENSHIFT_BASE_URL and OPENSHIFT_TOKEN env vars, which only set the flat cluster (#88 item 3)
divergences.toil: TOIL_OPENSHIFT_* env vars configure the default connection and win over anything stored for it. Another connection takes only its own TOIL_CONN_<NAME>_* variables, then defaults.openshift; the TOIL_OPENSHIFT_* token never fills a gap in it
divergences.why: Env vars outrank every stored value, and a credential goes only to the connection it's configured on.

divergences.old: openshift cluster list reading every named and flat cluster from config as { count, clusters[{ environment, instance, baseUrl }], defaultEnvironment, defaultInstance }
divergences.toil: An alias of toil connections list --area openshift (CLI only; over MCP, the connections_list tool with area openshift). It lists every openshift connection, so every configured cluster, as { configFile, connections[{ name, area, isDefault, host, writes, values }] }: a cluster's env and instance settings are in values (where each came from, never the value), isDefault marks the default, and host stands for baseUrl. It never prints a secret
divergences.why: Clusters are connections, and listing connections is core's job: an area command never sees the config, so no area can read another connection's settings (CLAUDE.md, Commands never read config or env).

divergences.old: openshift pod logs failing at once on HTTP 429, with no retry
divergences.toil: A 429 is retried as on every other request (honouring Retry-After up to 30 s, three attempts) before failing with HTTP
divergences.why: Every request goes through core's one HTTP layer, which retries a 429 the same way for every command.
